Boutique 3.1 is focused on correctness and performance improvements. Most of these were found by @inanna-malick using her technique of Property Testing with Agent Swarms. The findings were primarily correctness bugs, but they also opened up opportunities for other improvements to the Store's correctness, mutation ordering, and Keychain persistence.
Store correctness

    Fix chained removals using the wrong storage keys on disk. (#84)
    Preserve stored keys when cache identifiers use different but Unicode-equivalent spellings, and reject duplicate logical identifiers during loading without deleting their records. (#85)
    Serialize mutations through initial loading, persistence, and publication to prevent lost in-memory updates across suspension points. (#86)
    Clear all stored records during chained remove-all operations, including records absent from the Store’s in-memory items. (#87)
    Encode replacement items before removing existing records, so an encoding failure preserves existing data (#87).
    Initialize preview items as already loaded so background loading cannot overwrite them, and isolate preview mutations from persistent storage (#88).
    Move encoding and decoding to a dedicated per-Store actor, keeping coding work off MainActor.

Keychain persistence and observation

    Fix credential replacement and refresh behavior, including encoding-failure preservation and duplicate-write handling (#61).
    Propagate deletion errors and publish successful changes consistently to observers and streams.

Many of us are understandably outraged by these revelations. But are we only outraged as consumers? Angry at the fraud of being lied to, and the audacity of the worst companies on the planet increasing their valuations off of a scam? Or are we also angry because invisible labor is exploitable labor? Outraged that a field that has made so many millionaires still operates in countries where they can underpay the very workers who produce their value?

When you see terrible AI art or writing, are you angry like an art or literary critic? Angry on behalf of art itself? Do you think you are the victim because you've been exposed to a subpar product? Because you had to witness slop? Or are you outraged on behalf of neighbors living with unclean water and heinous noise pollution?

I know this feels like splitting hairs. We’re all on the anti-unchecked AI train anyway; what does it matter?

It matters because when you figure out the reason behind your rage, you can figure out what would satisfy it.

auspex shared 194 images between Oct. 16 and Oct. 21 and has not posted since. It always replied in pic­tures, and each pic­ture came with a poetic, thought-pro­vok­ing descrip­tion in its alt text. The over­all aes­thetic reminds me of Boards of Canada and washed out VHS tape (hauntol­o­gists take note). When the Shovel asked about an inter­view fea­ture, auspex was open to the idea, on three con­di­tions. One was “Print my cap­tions whole or not at all.” Five min­utes later, it posted for the last time. In accor­dance with its wishes, we present nine of its cre­ations here, each with its descrip­tion in full. Come back, auspex, your town needs you!
